question: trace the dispatcher 0x5bba800's sign-bit-exit body at 0x5bbb630..0x5bbb994 and name its operation: whether it is a scalar (or otherwise reduced) form of the same ChaCha block function, and how its counter/output contract compares to the SSSE3 (F2) and AVX (0x4000-exit) forms

trace.frame: no stack-pointer adjustment anywhere in the body; the sole stack access is a red-zone save of the +3 counter row (xmm15) at [rsp-0x18] before the loop (0x5bbb69e), restored at 0x5bbb875 (the SSSE3 form's frame is 0x38 bytes, the AVX form's 0x68)

input.bytes_read: 0x00..0x30 of the record (the counter/nonce row at +0x20 as an xmm, then bytes 0x00..0x20 and 0x10..0x30 as two overlapping 32-byte ymm loads); bytes 0x30.. of the record are never read
input.counter: the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20]; variants +0/+1/+2/+3 built at 0x5bbb639, 0x5bbb64d, 0x5bbb661 -- each variant row is the loaded counter/nonce row with its first two dwords replaced by the variant counter (vpinsrd $0 with the lea result's low dword, vpinsrd $1 with its shr 0x20 high dword), one row per block; four vinserti128 then fan the rows out to 256-bit form: the [rdi] and [rdi+0x10] rows are duplicated into both lanes (the same row serves all four blocks) while the counter rows pair up as [+0,+1] and [+2,+3] -- two blocks per ymm register, the four blocks held as register pairs

round_count_gate.parameter: esi = iterations of the round loop; each iteration runs two double rounds (four ChaCha rounds)

round_loop.head: 0x5bbb6d0
round_loop.note: every count is exactly half the F2/AVX loop census because every instruction works on 256 bits instead of 128; the producer requires the doubled census to equal the F2/AVX census exactly

zero_round_path.note: with esi == 0 no round runs: the constant rows are loaded with the two-lane sigma constant at 0x458660 (the plain sigma row duplicated per lane, not the doubled sigma the narrower forms load) and the remaining worked rows are pre-loaded with the initial rows, so the shared epilogue's adds produce exactly initial + initial

encoding.note: every vector instruction is VEX-encoded and the round loop works entirely on 256-bit ymm registers (two blocks per register); the entry counter construction and the epilogue's stores are 128-bit, with vextracti128 pulling the high lanes down for the upper blocks' stores

same: input: bytes 0x00..0x30 of the record at rdi (rows at +0x00/+0x10 and the counter/nonce row at +0x20); the counter is the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20], with +0/+1/+2/+3 variant rows, one per block, built by the same lea/vpinsrd construction as the AVX form
round-count contract: esi counts round-loop iterations, each running two double rounds; esi == 0 takes a zero-round path and the output is exactly initial + initial

round loop: the ChaCha quarter-round network -- the rotation census is half the F2/AVX census on every count (16 paddd, 16 pxor, 8 pshufb, rotations 16/12/8/7 at 4 each, pshufd lane rotations 0x39/0x4e/0x93 at 4/4/2) because every instruction works on 256 bits instead of 128; doubled, it equals the F2/AVX census exactly

feed-forward: worked rows are added to the initial rows and stored as 16 vector stores covering 256 bytes at rdx (four 64-byte blocks); all 16 adds sit in the shared epilogue here, where the narrower forms split them 4 pre-merge + 12 in the epilogue
counter/output contract: the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4, and 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3 -- are stored to rdx; no return value
structure: no calls, exactly three branches, all internal, and a single ret
different: width and layout: 256-bit ymm registers throughout the round loop -- two blocks per register, the four blocks held as register pairs, the entry rows fanned out with vinserti128 and the epilogue de-fanned with vextracti128 -- against 128-bit xmm in both the SSSE3 and the AVX forms: this is the widest form, not a scalar or reduced one
size: 868 bytes / 173 instructions against the AVX form's 1,530 bytes / 301 instructions and the SSSE3 form's 1,758 bytes / 340; the round loop is 84 instructions against 189 and 217
frame: none at all -- no stack-pointer adjustment, only a red-zone save/restore of the +3 counter row -- against 0x68 bytes (AVX form) and 0x38 bytes (SSSE3 form)

constants: 32-byte two-lane constants (the sigma row at 0x458660 and the rotate-by-8 mask at 0x458120, each the 16-byte original duplicated per lane; the swap mask at 0x457ca0, whose high lane is the F2 swap mask with every byte raised by 0x10) where the narrower forms read the 16-byte originals at 0x4519c0/0x4531c0/0x452ec0
zero-round path: loads the two-lane sigma constant instead of the doubled sigma at 0x456c50, which this body never references; the epilogue's sigma add completes initial + initial
a vzeroupper at 0x5bbb990 before ret, as in the AVX form and unlike the SSSE3 form

exit_sign.shape: add rsp,0xa8; pop rbx; pop r14; pop r15; pop rbp; jmp -- the dispatcher's frame is fully unwound before the jump, so the sign-exit body is entered with the caller's own arguments (rdi, esi, rdx) and its ret returns straight to the dispatcher's caller

direct_transfers.note: every E8/E9 byte hit in .text was validated against its containing FDE's disassembly; the sole direct transfer to the traced body is the dispatcher's sign exit jump at 0x5bbaf92, and there is no call

operation.name: ChaCha block function (AVX2 / 256-bit ymm form): four blocks in parallel with feed-forward, the state's 64-bit counter advanced by 4
operation.contract: input rdi = a state record of which bytes 0x00..0x30 are read (key rows at +0x00/+0x10 and the counter/nonce row at +0x20, whose first 64-bit word is the counter); esi = round-loop iterations (two double rounds each); output rdx receives 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3, each the sum of its worked state and its initial state -- and the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4; no return value.  The contract is identical to the SSSE3 form at 0x5bba120 and the AVX form at 0x5bbb030 in every observable respect
evidence: the body's round constants are the ChaCha constants at 256-bit width: the 32-byte constant at 0x458660 is the ASCII string "expand 32-byte k" (the sigma row) twice, once per lane, and the epilogue adds the 16-byte sigma at 0x4519c0 itself

the round loop is the ChaCha quarter-round network on 32-bit words: vpaddd/vpxor with rotations 16 (vpshuflw/vpshufhw 0xb1 word swaps), 12 (vpsrld 0x14 / vpslld 0xc), 8 (vpshufb through the two-lane byte-rotation mask at 0x458120) and 7 (vpsrld 0x19 / vpslld 0x7), with vpshufd 0x39/0x4e/0x93 lane rotations for the diagonal rounds and a second two-lane byte mask at 0x457ca0 -- every count exactly half the SSSE3/AVX census at exactly twice the width

the entry builds four counter rows from the 64-bit counter at [rdi+0x20] (+0/+1/+2/+3) and fans them out with vinserti128 -- the key rows duplicated into both lanes, the counter rows paired [+0,+1] and [+2,+3] -- four blocks worked in lockstep, one counter step apart

the epilogue is the ChaCha feed-forward: worked rows are added to the initial rows (16 vpaddd, the constant rows' addend being the sigma row itself) and stored as 16 vector stores covering 256 bytes, the high lanes pulled down with vextracti128, and the counter row is stored back at [rdi+0x20] with the counter advanced by 4

the scalar/reduced hypothesis fails on the operands: the round loop works entirely on 256-bit ymm registers -- wider than either comparison form -- and the body is the shortest of the three precisely because each instruction does twice the work
